bull.b: Minimal debt reduces fixed financial obligations and preserves flexibility while Chemomab advances its clinical programs. A lightly leveraged balance sheet can lessen refinancing pressure and allow more of the available capital to support research rather than interest payments.

The 2025 improvement in losses and cash consumption indicates some expense discipline despite the company remaining early stage. If maintained, lower burn could extend operational runway and make future financing requirements more manageable as development programs progress.

A focused therapeutic strategy around fibro-inflammatory diseases and CCL24 gives Chemomab a defined scientific identity rather than a broad, diffuse portfolio. Progress in these targeted programs could support durable differentiation if clinical results validate the mechanism.

bear.b: The absence of revenue means Chemomab has not yet demonstrated commercial traction or an operating model capable of funding itself. Its financial outlook therefore remains dependent on clinical progress and eventual product success rather than established customer demand.

Sustained negative operating and free cash flow requires Chemomab to keep funding research and operations through external capital. That dependence can constrain development choices and increase financing risk if the company cannot reach meaningful clinical or commercial milestones.

Shrinking assets and equity show that cumulative losses are consuming the company’s financial base rather than building productive scale. Continued deterioration could increase value dilution risk and reduce the resources available to sustain its clinical pipeline.
